title: Assign Row Numbers Within Department Groups
description: Assign each employee a **seniority rank within their department** based on hire date (1 = earliest hire = most senior). Show emp_id, name, department, hire_date, and dept_seniority_rank.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (emp_id INT, name VARCHAR(100), department VARCHAR(50), hire_date DATE); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering','2020-03-15'),(2,'Bob','Engineering','2022-07-01'),(3,'Carol','Engineering','2021-11-20'),(4,'Dave','Marketing','2019-05-10'),(5,'Eve','Marketing','2023-01-15'),(6,'Frank','Marketing','2021-08-22'),(7,'Grace','Sales','2018-06-01'),(8,'Hank','Sales','2020-09-15'),(9,'Ivy','Sales','2022-04-10'),(10,'Jack','Sales','2019-12-05');
solution_sql: SELECT emp_id, name, department, hire_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY hire_date) AS dept_seniority_rank FROM employees ORDER BY department, hire_date

test_cases.description: 10 employees with seniority ranks 1-3 in Engineering, 1-3 in Marketing, 1-4 in Sales — based on hire_date ascending.

hints: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY hire_date) — partitioning by department causes the numbering to restart at 1 for each department.
Ordering by hire_date ASC means the earliest hire gets rank 1 (most senior); the latest hire gets the highest rank number.
explanation: ROW_NUMBER() restarts at 1 for each new PARTITION value. Engineering: Alice (Mar 2020)=1, Carol (Nov 2021)=2, Bob (Jul 2022)=3. Marketing: Dave (May 2019)=1, Frank (Aug 2021)=2, Eve (Jan 2023)=3. Sales: Grace (Jun 2018)=1, Jack (Dec 2019)=2, Hank (Sep 2020)=3, Ivy (Apr 2022)=4. Unlike RANK, ROW_NUMBER never has ties — two people hired the same day would get different sequential numbers.
